checks.do: When a plan is rejected, check the rule's method first, then the field named in the error.

When a rule exists but forwards unexpectedly, read its `forwardMethod` from the tenant before reasoning about its other fields, since the method decides which of them are required, allowed or ignored.

console-methods.statement: The console offers these forwarding methods: ZPA (to a Private Access App Connector through the Private Access gateway), Direct, Proxy Chaining (to a third-party proxy service), Dedicated IP (through a dedicated IP gateway) and GeoIP (source IP address mapped to the location of the originating request).

quotes: Forwarding Method: From the drop-down menu, choose ZPA to forward the traffic to a Private Access App Connector through the Private Access gateway
Forwarding Method: From the drop-down menu, choose Proxy Chaining to forward the traffic to a third-party proxy service.
Forwarding Method: From the drop-down menu, choose Dedicated IP to forward the traffic through a dedicated IP gateway.
Forwarding Method: From the drop-down menu, choose GeoIP to forward traffic with the source IP address mapped to the location of the originating request.
Select Direct to directly forward the traffic to the destination server using the Zscaler service IP address.
evidence.after: choose Proxy Chaining to forward the traffic to a third-party proxy service.

direct-meaning.statement: Direct forwards the traffic to the destination server using the Zscaler service IP address.

quotes: Select Direct to directly forward the traffic to the destination server using the Zscaler service IP address.

enum-values.statement: The Terraform provider accepts ten `forward_method` values: INVALID, DIRECT, PROXYCHAIN, ZIA, ZPA, ECZPA, ECSELF, DROP, ENATDEDIP and GEOIP. The Python SDK's add-rule docstring lists the same ten; its update-rule docstring lists only the first eight.

tf-doc-meanings.statement: The Terraform documentation describes ENATDEDIP as the Dedicated IP method and GEOIP as Zscaler automatically selecting the nearest data center from the data center mappings on the Geo IP page. The documentation also says ZPA requires `zpa_gateway` and `zpa_app_segments`, and PROXYCHAIN requires `proxy_gateway`.

quotes: `ENATDEDIP` - Dedicated IP method.
`GEOIP` - Zscaler automatically selects the nearest data center to forward the traffic based on the data center mappings in the Geo IP page.
If forward_method is `ZPA` the attributes `zpa_gateway` and `zpa_app_segments` are required.
If forward_method is `PROXYCHAIN` the attributes `proxy_gateway` is required.

dedicated-ip-gateway.statement: A Dedicated IP rule chooses a dedicated IP gateway; selecting the Default gateway lets the Zscaler service pick the optimal data center. The default gateway is created when dedicated IP addresses are allocated, cannot be edited or deleted, and directs traffic to the geographically nearest data center that has a dedicated IP address assigned.

quotes: Forward to Gateway: Choose the appropriate dedicated IP gateway. Select Default gateway to allow the Zscaler service to automatically choose the optimal data center based on your location.
When dedicated IP addresses are allocated to your organization, the Zscaler service creates a default gateway that can neither be edited nor deleted.
the Zscaler service directs the traffic to the geographically nearest data center that has a dedicated IP address assigned.

provider-field-requirements.statement: At plan time, for rules of type FORWARDING, the provider requires `zpa_app_segments` and `zpa_gateway` when the method is ZPA; requires `proxy_gateway` when it is PROXYCHAIN; and rejects `zpa_gateway`, `proxy_gateway`, `zpa_app_segments`, `zpa_application_segments` and `zpa_application_segment_groups` when it is DIRECT (PROXYCHAIN rejects the ZPA ones). These checks do not run for other methods or other rule types.

dest-fields-gate.statement: The provider rejects `dest_addresses`, `dest_countries` and `dest_ip_categories` on any rule whose method is not PROXYCHAIN, DIRECT, ENATDEDIP or GEOIP. That excludes ZIA, ZPA, ECZPA, ECSELF, DROP and INVALID, not only ZPA, and the check is outside the type-FORWARDING condition.

provider-exceeds-console.statement: The Terraform provider's accepted forward_method values include INVALID, ZIA, ECZPA, ECSELF and DROP, none of which is among the methods the console offers (ZPA, Direct, Proxy Chaining, Dedicated IP, GeoIP).
provider-exceeds-console.conditions: Compares the provider's value list with the console method list captured from the help page; the help page lists the drop-down choices but does not say the list is exhaustive.

positions.says: The published ZIA OpenAPI contract for creating a forwarding rule lists eight values and not ENATDEDIP or GEOIP.

positions.says: The Terraform provider accepts ten values, adding ENATDEDIP and GEOIP, and the console offers Dedicated IP and GeoIP methods.

contract-enum.impact: Do not treat ENATDEDIP or GEOIP as invalid because the contract omits them, nor assume the API accepts every value the provider validates. Read existing rules from the tenant to see which values occur.

method-semantics.title: What ZIA, DROP, ECSELF and INVALID do
method-semantics.detail: Unverified legacy statement: ZIA is "Default egress via Zscaler's cloud egress IPs. No special config required"; DROP is "Silently discard matching traffic"; ECSELF is "Cloud Connector self-forwarding"; INVALID is a "Placeholder / unconfigured state - not a valid production action"; PROXYCHAIN is "Forward to a downstream proxy" (the console help says third-party proxy service, so that one is now sourced). The console help lists no ZIA, Drop or ECSELF method, and the Terraform and SDK sources give only the value names. Resolve with a lab rule per value, or a vendor article that names them.
method-semantics.blocks: explaining the effect of a rule whose forwardMethod is ZIA, DROP, ECSELF or INVALID

no-match-default.title: What happens to traffic that matches no Forwarding Control rule
no-match-default.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Default when no rule matches: traffic falls to the `ZIA` forward method - standard ZIA cloud egress. There is no implicit drop." No captured source states a default or an implicit drop. Resolve by a lab trace of traffic matching no rule, or a vendor statement.
